author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Three jurors from Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial have described the deliberations that ended in a mistrial, offering a new account of the panel’s internal deadlock.

The jury foreperson and two other panelists told NBC10 Boston that one juror would not join the rest of the panel in a verdict. They said deliberations became tense and that several jurors changed their views while reviewing the evidence and competing arguments about criminal responsibility.

Their interview reflects the recollections of three jurors, not a formal court finding about every member of the panel. NBC10 Boston said it tried to contact the juror described by the others as the holdout.

A judge declared the mistrial last week after the jury reported it could not reach a unanimous decision. The case remains unresolved, and prosecutors and the court must determine the next procedural steps. Nothing said after the mistrial changes the presumption of innocence or constitutes a verdict. The interview is significant because it adds firsthand context to the note and courtroom discussions that preceded the judge’s decision.
dek: The jury foreperson and two other panelists told NBC10 Boston that one holdout prevented agreement in the closely watched murder case.
headline: Three Lindsay Clancy jurors describe deadlock after mistrial
